title: Holy Father, Thou Hast Taught Me
description: Holy Father, Thou Hast Taught Me in Tonic Solfa to LUX EOI, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 528, “Dedication to God”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens Double (8.7.8.7 D) (8.7.8.7.8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to LUX EOI; any other Eights and Sevens Double (8.7.8.7 D) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ho-ly Fa-ther, Thou hast taught me I should live to Thee a-lone; Year by year, Thy hand hath brought me On through dan-gers oft un-known. When I wan-dered, Thou hast found me; When I doubt-ed, sent me light; Still Thine arm has been a-round me, All my paths were in Thy sight.

lines: Holy Father, Thou hast taught me
I should live to Thee alone;
Year by year, Thy hand hath brought me
On through dangers oft unknown.
When I wandered, Thou hast found me;
When I doubted, sent me light;
Still Thine arm has been around me,
All my paths were in Thy sight.
In the world will foes assail me,
Craftier, stronger far than I;
And the strife may never fail me,
Well I know, before I die.
Therefore, Lord, I come, believing
Thou canst give the power I need;
Through the prayer of faith receiving
Strength, — the spirit's strength indeed.
I would trust in Thy protecting,
Wholly rest upon Thine arm,
Follow wholly Thy directing,
Thou mine only guard from harm!
Keep me from mine own undoing,
Help me turn to Thee when tried,
Still my footsteps, Father, viewing,
Keep me ever at Thy side!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1866.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to LUX EOI by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
